subject: Discovery recap — tracing hooks, golden prompts & rollout criteria
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole>, Dev Patel <dev_patel>
Date: Wed, 01 Apr 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap — tracing hooks, golden prompts & rollout criteria

Hi Elena — thanks again for the intro call today. Quick recap from our side to make sure we captured the priorities and to propose next steps. Please tell me if I missed anything.

Pain points you shared:
- Limited observability on prompt-level regressions: engineering only sees latency/cost but not per-prompt quality drift.
- Rollouts are high-risk: past rollouts produced cost spikes and occasional hallucination regressions that were hard to trace.
- Need for clear canary/fallback guardrails and a fast way to detect regressions tied to prompt families.

Current stack (as I heard it):
- Model hosting: internal k8s cluster using an in-house endpoint manager (runs open models).
- Monitoring: Datadog for infra metrics, Mixpanel for feature events.
- CI/infra: Terraform + GitOps, KMS from AWS.

Success criteria you mentioned for a POC:
- Traceable per-request lineage (prompt version -> model variant -> response) surfaced in dashboards.
- Regression alerts that fire on seeded tests (golden prompt set) within 24 hours.
- Per-route token cost + 95p latency dashboard, plus a per-prompt quality metric (simple pass/fail on golden prompts).
- Ability to perform canary rollouts with automatic fallback to previous model variant on quality regressions.

Specific observability & evals asks from the call:
- Dashboard set: (1) per-route latency/cost, (2) per-prompt quality trends, (3) rollout health (canary vs baseline).
- Tracing hooks: we will need an integration to attach a trace id and prompt metadata to every request and map it to model variant/KV cache hits.
- Golden prompt sets: you asked for a way to upload and run golden prompts automatically against new model variants with regression alerting.
- Regression alerting: configurable thresholds (absolute and relative) and on-call paging integration.

Attachments (shared with this email): acme_golden_prompts_v1.csv, current_arch_diagram.pdf — please confirm you intended to share these with our tech team.

Proposed next steps:
1) Schedule a technical deep-dive (Marissa and Dev to join) for 60–90m where we walk tracing instrumentation and the dashboard templates.
2) Acme to share a canonical golden prompt CSV + a short seed dataset (anonymized) we can use for seeded regression tests.
3) Redwood will spin up a sandbox POC environment (50k tokens/day suggested) and deliver the baseline dashboards and a tracing hook snippet for your team to validate.

Suggested time windows (PST): Thu 2026-04-02 09:30–11:00 or Fri 2026-04-03 13:00–14:30. Which works best?

Thanks — looking forward.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmeai.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole>, Dev Patel <dev_patel>
Date: Wed, 01 Apr 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — tracing hooks, golden prompts & rollout criteria

Thanks Sergio — this captures the discussion well. A couple of follow-ups / clarifications from my side:

- Compliance & data concerns: we will need KMS integration for any payloads stored in the sandbox. PII must be redacted; we can provide an anonymized seed.
- On-prem vs cloud: we'll evaluate both but for the POC cloud sandbox is preferred.
- Acceptance timeline: we want to run the seeded regression suite over three successive model variants and see consistent alerting before proceeding to a production rollout.
- Can you confirm whether the tracing hooks will include a stable request id we can map back into our internal feature logs? That's a must for the SRE team.

We prefer Thu 04/02 09:30–11:00 PST. If you can get a short agenda and the deep-dive dial-in, I'll invite my SRE and product owners.

Elena
Elena Torres
Director of ML Platforms, Acme AI
elena.torres@acmeai.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole>, Dev Patel <dev_patel>
Date: Thu, 02 Apr 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — tracing hooks, golden prompts & rollout criteria

Perfect — booked Thu 04/02 09:30 PST. I created a short agenda below and added the meeting invite.

Agenda (60–75m):
- 10m: goals & success criteria alignment (Sergio + Elena)
- 15m: high-level tracing/metadata model and DKMS/KMS notes (Dev)
- 25m: dashboard walkthrough + golden prompt runbook (Marissa)
- 15m: POC acceptance criteria, timeline, and next steps

POC acceptance criteria (proposal):
- Tracing: every request in sandbox contains a stable trace_id and prompt_version tag that is visible in Redwood traces and map-able to your logs.
- Dashboards: per-route latency/cost and per-prompt quality dashboard live in the sandbox and populated with seeded runs.
- Regression detection: seeded golden prompts cause a regression alert when a variant drops below the agreed quality threshold (configurable).
- Rollout guardrail: canary traffic routing and automatic fallback policy demoed end-to-end.

Action items assigned:
- Acme (Elena): share anonymized golden prompt CSV + small sample dataset before EOD Wed 04/01 (we received acme_golden_prompts_v1.csv — thanks, we'll validate format).
- Redwood (Marissa, Dev): prepare dashboard templates and a tracing hook snippet to share pre-call.
- Sergio: send calendar invite + agenda (done).

Marissa and Dev — can you drop the tracing hook snippet and dashboard links in the thread so Elena's SREs can skim before the call?

Best,
Sergio

Quick pre-read: attaching a small tracing hook snippet and example Span schema. This will show how we attach trace_id, prompt_version, route, and cache_hit to each request.

On the call we'll demo the snippet against a toy endpoint and show how the trace_id maps back into Datadog/Apm and our per-prompt quality dashboard.
